spec.description: Subscribe to order status and execution events for this account -- a unified stream replacing WebSocket v1's separate `openOrders` and `ownTrades` channels.

snap_trades.description: If true, the last 50 order fills are included in the snapshot.

snap_orders.description: If true, open orders are included in the snapshot.

order_status.description: If true, all possible order-status transitions are streamed. Otherwise, only open/close transitions are streamed: `new`, `filled`, `canceled`, `expired`.

rebased.description: Effective for viewing xstocks only. If true, display in terms of underlying equity, otherwise in terms of SPV tokens.

ratecounter.description: If true, the rate-limit counter is included in the stream.

users.description: Available on master accounts only. If `all`, events for master and subaccounts are streamed and no snapshot is provided; otherwise only master account events are published.

snapshot_trades.description: If true, the snapshot provides only trade events. Otherwise, open orders and trades are both included in the snapshot. Deprecated -- use `snap_trades`.

snapshot.description: Request a snapshot after subscribing. Deprecated -- use `snap_orders` or `snap_trades`.

payload.title: ExecutionsMessage
payload.description: An executions channel push -- a snapshot of open orders and recent fills right after subscribing, then one push per order status transition or fill. The snapshot and update stream share the same data schema; the fields present in each report depend on `exec_type`.

data.description: A list of execution reports: order status transitions and fills.

anyOf.title: ExecutionTradeEvent
anyOf.description: An execution report for a fill (`exec_type: "trade"`).

order_id.description: Unique order identifier generated by Kraken.

order_userref.description: Optional numeric client identifier associated with one or more orders.

cl_ord_id.description: Optional client identifier associated with the order.

symbol.description: The symbol of the currency pair, e.g. `BTC/USD`.

order_type.description: The execution model of the order.

fee_usd_equiv.description: The total fee paid, in USD.

fee_ccy_pref.description: The preferred currency for paying fees. `fcib`: prefer fee in base currency. `fciq`: prefer fee in quote currency.

liquidated.description: Indicates if the order has been liquidated by the engine.

sender_sub_id.description: For institutional accounts, identifies the underlying sub-account/trader for Self Trade Prevention (STP).

user.description: The Kraken-generated identifier for a user / sub-account. Only published when the subscription requested `users: "all"`.

ext_ord_id.description: An optional, external partner order identifier shown on order events.

amended.description: Indicates if the order has been amended -- the modification history can be extracted from the REST `OrderAmends` endpoint. Present on the snapshot and on `amended`/`restated` event types.

ext_exec_id.description: An optional, external partner execution identifier shown on trade events.

last_price.description: The average price in this trade event.

last_qty.description: The quantity filled in this trade event.

fees.description: The fees paid on this trade event. Currently expressed in the quote currency only.

items.title: ExecutionFee
items.description: One fee component paid on a trade execution.

margin.description: Indicates if the order can be funded on margin.

margin_borrow.description: Indicates if this execution is on margin, i.e. if the trade increased or reduced the size of margin borrowing.

position_status.description: Status of the position on a margin order.

anyOf.title: ExecutionOrderEvent
anyOf.description: An execution report for an order lifecycle transition -- everything other than a fill: the order being received, going live, refilling (iceberg), being canceled/expired, amended, restated by the engine, or otherwise updated.

order_id.description: Unique order identifier generated by Kraken.

order_userref.description: Optional numeric client identifier associated with one or more orders.

cl_ord_id.description: Optional client identifier associated with the order.

exec_type.description: The kind of order-lifecycle event. `pending_new`: order received and validated but not yet live. `new`: order created and live in the engine. `filled`: order fully filled. `iceberg_refill`: an iceberg order refill. `canceled`: order cancelled. `expired`: order expired. `amended`: user-initiated amend, e.g. limit price change. `restated`: engine-initiated amend for maintenance of position or book (see `reason`), e.g. reducing non-tradable liquidity. `status`: an order status update, e.g. trigger price changed.

symbol.description: The symbol of the currency pair, e.g. `BTC/USD`.

order_type.description: The execution model of the order.

fee_usd_equiv.description: The total fee paid, in USD.

fee_ccy_pref.description: The preferred currency for paying fees. `fcib`: prefer fee in base currency. `fciq`: prefer fee in quote currency.

liquidated.description: Indicates if the order has been liquidated by the engine.

sender_sub_id.description: For institutional accounts, identifies the underlying sub-account/trader for Self Trade Prevention (STP).

user.description: The Kraken-generated identifier for a user / sub-account. Only published when the subscription requested `users: "all"`.

ext_ord_id.description: An optional, external partner order identifier shown on order events.

amended.description: Indicates if the order has been amended -- the modification history can be extracted from the REST `OrderAmends` endpoint. Present on the snapshot and on `amended`/`restated` event types.

cash_order_qty.description: Order volume expressed in quote currency, if specified on the original order.

display_qty.description: Display quantity for iceberg order types.

display_qty_remain.description: Indicates the next `display_qty` in an iceberg order.

limit_price.description: Limit price, for order types that support a limit price restriction.

time_in_force.description: How long an order remains in effect before being expired. `GTC`: Good Till Canceled. `GTD`: Good Till Date. `IOC`: Immediate Or Cancel. `FOK`: Fill Or Kill.

effective_time.description: Scheduled start time of the order. RFC3339, e.g. `2022-12-25T09:30:59.123456Z`.

expire_time.description: Scheduled expiration time of the order. RFC3339, e.g. `2022-12-25T09:30:59.123456Z`.

no_mpp.description: Indicates if the order has market price protection.

ord_ref_id.description: Referral order transaction id that created this order.

reason.description: The reason associated with the event, if applicable.

contingent.title: ExecutionContingent
contingent.description: Template for the secondary close order(s) generated when the primary order fills.

order_type.description: The order type of the secondary order(s) created on each fill.

trigger_price.description: Trigger price amount on the secondary order(s), only on triggered secondary order types. Combined with `trigger_price_type` to determine the effective trigger price.

trigger_price_type.description: Trigger price units on the secondary order(s), only on triggered secondary order types. `static`: a static market price, e.g. 30000 for BTC/USD. `pct`: a percentage offset from the reference price, e.g. -10% from index price. `quote`: a notional offset from the reference price in the quote currency, e.g. 150 BTC/USD from last price.

limit_price.description: Limit price amount on the secondary order(s), only on secondary order types that support a limit price. Combined with `limit_price_type` to determine the effective limit price.

limit_price_type.description: Limit price units on the secondary order(s), only on secondary order types that support a limit price. `static`: a static market price, e.g. 30000 for BTC/USD. `pct`: a percentage offset from the reference price, e.g. -10% from index price. `quote`: a notional offset from the reference price in the quote currency, e.g. 150 BTC/USD from last price.

triggers.title: ExecutionTrigger
triggers.description: Parameters and status of the price trigger for a triggered order type.

reference.description: The reference price tracked for triggering the order.

price.description: Amount for the trigger price -- supports both static market prices and relative prices. Combined with `price_type` to determine the effective trigger price.

price_type.description: Units for the trigger price. `static`: a static market price, e.g. 30000 for BTC/USD. `pct`: a percentage offset from the reference price, e.g. -10% from index price. `quote`: a notional offset from the reference price in the quote currency, e.g. 150 BTC/USD from last price.

actual_price.description: The current value of the effective trigger price -- useful when the trigger was entered as a relative price or the trigger price changes over time.

peak_price.description: The peak / trough price on `trailing-stop` and `trailing-stop-limit` orders.

last_price.description: On trigger activation, the value of the reference last price that triggered the order.

status.description: Set to `triggered` once the trigger conditions are met and the order becomes active.

timestamp.description: On trigger activation, the timestamp of the trigger event. RFC3339, e.g. `2022-12-25T09:30:59.123456Z`.

stop_price.description: The stop price for triggered order types. Deprecated -- use `triggers`.

trigger.description: Reference price for triggered order types. Deprecated -- use `triggers`.

triggered_price.description: Price which triggered the order. Deprecated -- use `triggers`.

notes: Private channel over wss://ws-auth.kraken.com/v2 -- requires a token obtained via REST GetWebSocketsToken. `channel` and `token` are omitted from the subscribe requestBody schema, same judgment call as `streams.private.balances`: `channel` is fixed (carried as `spec.channel`) and `token` is injected by the transport, not a caller-supplied parameter.
Unifies WS v1's `openOrders` and `ownTrades` channels; `data` items are order-status and fill reports sharing one schema whose actual field set depends on `exec_type`.

`data` items are modeled as anyOf[ExecutionTradeEvent, ExecutionOrderEvent] rather than a full 10-way split by `exec_type`. The docs explicitly scope a handful of fields to 'trade events only' (`cost`, `exec_id`, `fees`, `last_price`, `last_qty`, and by implication `trade_id`/`liquidity_ind`/`margin_borrow`), which is the one genuinely documented field-presence boundary in this shape -- so that boundary is what splits the anyOf. The other 9 `exec_type` values (`pending_new`, `new`, `filled`, `iceberg_refill`, `canceled`, `expired`, `amended`, `restated`, `status`) have no per-type field documentation beyond the `amended` field's own note (present on the snapshot and on `amended`/`restated` events); splitting further would mean guessing which of ~30 undifferentiated fields apply to which of those 9 types, which the docs don't state. Flagging in case a captured example later reveals a real per-type field boundary worth splitting on.

`limit_price_type` appears as a top-level field in the doc's 'Pending' example JSON but has no corresponding top-level ResponseField entry (it's only documented nested under `contingent.limit_price_type`) -- treated as a doc inconsistency and left out of the schema rather than guessed in; same for the example's top-level `stop_price`, which the docs list as a real (if deprecated) top-level field and which *is* included.

`order_status` and `exec_type` are both documented via a bulleted `* value: meaning` list rather than an explicit 'One of:' tag, but each enumerates a closed, fully-defined set -- treated as documented enums per rule 2, same as `fee_ccy_pref`'s two-value list.

Required fields on both `data` item variants are inferred from what's present across the three documented example payloads (Pending/Live Order/Execution), since no individual data-item field carries an explicit 'required' tag in the upstream docs -- only `order_id`/`exec_type`/`order_status`/`timestamp` are common to all three examples and thus required on both variants; the trade variant adds the fields the docs mark 'trade events only' as required, empirically confirmed present in the one Execution example.

The subscribe reply is split anyOf[ExecutionsSubscribeAck, ExecutionsSubscribeError] on `success`, since a failed subscribe carries `error` and no `result` -- same shape as the success/failure reply split rule documented for WS commands.
